reports.definition_of_done:
The docs do not agree on what "done" means. There are three competing end states, and none of the three roadmap documents is listed in docs/DocsIndex.md as live, roadmap or historical.
(1) docs/audits/2026-09-completion-roadmap.md (2026-09-05). Its objective (line 5) is a "runtime capable of autonomous self-extensions and validation with built-in agents, maintaining PRODUCT/CORE separation". Done means the M6 exit criteria (lines 624-636): M1-M5 closed, legal/privacy/security sign-off, collateral, a public launch at 0.2.0 and a first enterprise customer on autonomous Tier 0. M7, the Learning Harness, comes after that (lines 781-798).
(2) docs/marketing/product-boundary.md (CEO lock, 2026-09-19). It narrows the end state to "Ashlar governs behavior, not intelligence". Core is contracts, gate, receipts, packages, constrained composition, verification, provenance, model abstraction, and share plus re-verify. Autonomy, self-learning, Cloud PAYG and Forge GA are on HOLD, and the doc says "Autonomy is not required for the company to succeed. Live path: embed → gate → package → receipts → DP."
(3) docs/ProductsAndBusinessPlan.md §5.3 and docs/ProductFleetImplementationRoadmap.md. These set commercial exits: 3-5 paying orgs across at least two of Cloud, Private and Enterprise, a first annual Private customer, and a first paying Cloud customer.
CONTINUITY.md §1 adds "CLI and GUI, targeting AWS, Azure, and native platforms, with an optional self-extending runtime".
I scored against the completion roadmap's 41 numbered milestone exit checkboxes, the only countable list. I also report against the 2026-09-19 core list, which is the newest and is nearly met.
